input: Given /data/team_a.txt and /data/team_b.txt containing member names (one per line, already sorted), use the comm command to find: 1) Members only in Team A (print under 'Only Team A:'). 2) Members only in Team B (print under 'Only Team B:'). 3) Members in both teams (print under 'Both teams:'). Print the count of each group.

transcript.final_response:
Here is the breakdown of team members using the `comm` command along with the member counts for each group:

### Commands & Output

```bash
# 1) Members only in Team A
echo "Only Team A:"
comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
echo "Count: $(comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"

# 2) Members only in Team B
echo "Only Team B:"
comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
echo "Count: $(comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"

# 3) Members in both teams
echo "Both teams:"
comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
echo "Count: $(comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"
```

---

```
Count: 3
```
